proposals.title: Spatial Domain Identification Using Graph Neural Networks
proposals.summary: This analysis leverages graph neural networks to integrate spatial coordinates with gene expression profiles. By constructing a neighborhood graph based on tissue coordinates and employing message passing algorithms, the study aims to delineate distinct tissue domains and boundaries. The approach ensures that spatial proximity and transcriptional similarity are jointly considered, effectively identifying and validating functionally diverse cellular regions while preserving rare or transitional states.

proposals.title: Optimizing Latent Space Embeddings for Spatial Transcriptomics
proposals.summary: This analysis focuses on the development of a compact latent space that fuses gene expression data with spatial constraints. Utilizing methods such as variational autoencoders augmented with spatial regularization, researchers will compare different weighting strategies between transcriptional variance and spatial smoothness. The performance will be benchmarked by its ability to preserve local neighborhood structures and evelop improved visualization, clustering, and downstream biological interpretation.

proposals.title: Spatial Batch Correction Across Platforms
proposals.summary: This study targets the challenge of integrating data from various spatial transcriptomics platforms by developing a spatially aware batch correction strategy. The analysis involves aligning datasets using techniques like mutual nearest neighbors or adversarial networks that incorporate both gene expression and spatial neighbor graphs. Performance is evaluated based on the retention of biologically relevant spatial organization while effectively removing platform-specific artifacts.

proposals.title: Multi-Resolution Analysis of Tissue Architecture
proposals.summary: This analysis proposes a hierarchical approach to study tissue organization at multiple spatial scales. High-resolution datasets will be aggregated into coarser maps using dynamic spatial smoothing, preserving key molecular patterns without losing fine spatial boundaries. By comparing outcomes across resolutions, the study aims to elucidate how distinct anatomical and molecular structures manifest, providing insights into tissue organization and pathology.

proposals.title: Spatial Denoising and Dropout Recovery
proposals.summary: Addressing the sparsity and noise inherent in spatial transcriptomics data, this analysis employs spatially informed imputation techniques to recover dropout events. Using local neighborhood information, the method applies targeted smoothing and regression techniques to augment gene expression profiles. The approach is validated against known marker genes and spatial patterns, ensuring that critical boundaries are maintained while reducing noise.

proposals.title: Trajectory Inference in Spatial Context
proposals.summary: This analysis integrates trajectory inference with spatial transcriptomics to map dynamic cellular state transitions within tissue sections. By combining pseudotime algorithms with spatial neighborhood constraints, the study will trace developmental or disease progression pathways. Computational methods will identify gradients and transitions, linking them to anatomical landmarks, thereby providing insights into lineage and spatial progression.

proposals.title: Spatially Coordinated Gene Co-expression Network Analysis
proposals.summary: This study is designed to build gene co-expression networks that are sensitive to spatial context. By calculating spatially weighted co-expression scores, the analysis identifies modules of genes that are co-regulated in specific tissue regions. This method not only highlights key regulatory circuits but also associates spatially localized expression patterns with underlying biological processes, enhancing the understanding of tissue micro-environments.

proposals.title: Comparative Evaluation of Spatial Embedding Methods
proposals.summary: This analysis systematically compares various embedding techniques for spatial transcriptomics, including expression-only, spatially smoothed, and hybrid approaches. By employing benchmark datasets with annotated tissue regions, the study quantifies performance based on metrics such as domain recovery accuracy, dropout correction efficacy, and preservation of spatial gradients. The goal is to determine which methods best capture the balance between transcriptional similarity and spatial continuity.
